feature: Join two caption lines, move a word back a line
summary: A caption broken in the wrong place can now be mended both ways: join a line with the next one, or carry a word (and the words before it) back onto the line before. Every word keeps its time and each fix is one undo.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open a talking screen recording and press Add Captions.
On the Captions track, right click the first line's bar and choose Join with Next Line.
Press Command Z, then Command Shift Z: the two lines come apart and join again.
Play into the second line, right click its first word on the picture, choose Move to Previous Line.
Right click any word of the first line: Move to Previous Line is there but dimmed.
Open Sequence > Caption Word in the menu bar: both rows are there, acting on the caption at the playhead.
Right click the Captions track, Export Subtitles > SubRip: the joined line is one subtitle.

evaluate: Is Join with Next Line where you reached for it, on the line's own bar, the way Premiere's Merge Captions is?
Does Move to Previous Line taking the clicked word AND every word before it match what you expected, as the mirror of Move to Next Line?
After a join, does the longer line read well on the picture, or would you want it split again by itself?
Is one undo per join or move the right size of step?
rough: No mock covers these menus: video-captions.html draws editing in place but no right click menu for a line or a word, so the rows sit beside the existing Move to Next Line and Start Here.
A joined line keeps the first line's box and wraps onto two rows on the picture when it is long (picture 2), even with the Captions panel's Lines set to 1; nothing re-splits it.
The walk chooses Move to Previous Line with a real right click on the word on the picture; the Join row is run from the line's menu as built, not by a right click at a spot on the track bar.
